short: task checks and the PR step engine
is: The machinery behind `zaf check` and `zaf verify`: the target (task or pull request), the model-free task check, and a threaded engine that runs `[check.<target>] steps` and dedupes their findings into a stored CheckRecord.
conventions: One module per step kind under step/: ci, command:<cmd>, runner:<name>:<role>, bot:<login>, codeql; a ?flagged suffix runs a step only for security-flagged tasks
Step reports speak `MUST: <path>:<line> <title>` and `NOTE: ...`; any other line is ignored
A task check uses no model: light gate, Tests: via [gate] tests, Architecture: ids as whole-word symbols in owned paths, Acceptance: lines listed as manual

fs.name: engine.rs
fs.role: each step in its own thread under one timeout

fs.name: step/
fs.role: step kinds: bot, ci, codeql, command, runner (each with tests)

fs.name: target.rs
fs.role: task issue number or pull request

notes: step/runner.rs writes assets/check/security.md as the brief when the role name contains `security`, else critique.md, and runs under the review profile
cli/check.rs stores the record under .zaf/runs/ and exits 0 clean, 1 must-fix, 2 step failure or missing backend
The ways repo's own ZAF.toml runs only the ci step for pull requests
